resource_measurement: CPU and memory are estimated by trapezoidal integration of Docker stats samples for all base and request-scoped containers matching the MCP target group. Integration starts at warmup start and ends at the detected cold-demand/supersession boundary or forced run cleanup. Overlapping discarded warmups for one group split that group's sampled integral equally. Samples are taken at the configured interval; attribution is estimated at group/container level, not directly measured per warmup process.
lifecycle_accounting: A predictive warmup is a predictive-stage prewarm_executor started event. It is marked used when a later ready event for the same target reports a running/resume startup mode and the predictive executor reports completion no later than that ready event. A started warmup with no matched demand is marked discarded at forced run cleanup; an earlier cold demand or superseding warmup provides an earlier discard-detection boundary, not a directly observed Docker removal timestamp.
attribution_limitations: The experiment runs the historical cumulative C1+C2 configuration. C1 prompt/stream prewarming remains enabled alongside predictive SDG; if both mechanisms target the same MCP group, timing and group-level Docker stats cannot causally separate their contribution.
hit_rate_accounting: Eligible sandbox requests are tool_group_activation_requested events whose group appeared as a predictive-stage prewarm_schedule candidate in that run, including activations that did not reach a ready event. A hit requires a running/resume mcp_server_ready event matched to a prior predictive warmup that had completed by readiness.
aggregation: Hit and false-positive rates pool numerators and denominators across completed sessions. Per-session discarded counts and resource integrals are pooled totals divided by completed sessions. Resource means include zero-cost sessions with no discarded warmups; records missing sufficient Docker samples are counted separately.
